item.title: Judgement day for Trump’s Republican Party
item.itunes:title: Judgement day for Trump’s Republican Party
item.itunes:subtitle: Voters go to the polls in today’s US midterm elections, widely seen as a referendum on the US president
item.description:
US voters head to the polls Tuesday to decide which party controls Congress and the FT’s James Politi breaks down the key Senate races to watch. Plus, oil investors and executives clash over future of Iran war.


Mentioned in this podcast:

US midterm elections 2026: The FT’s guide

Big majority of US voters disapprove of Trump’s handling of inflation: FT poll

Donald Trump’s imperial presidency faces a popular uprising

Oil tumbles on hopes for US-Iran talks

Gulf braced for escalation of war between US-Israel alliance and Iran

Credit: CNN, Haley Stevens, Associated Press, CSPAN, White House

item.title: The Gulf braces for new strikes against Iran
item.itunes:title: The Gulf braces for new strikes against Iran
item.itunes:subtitle: Diplomats warn that renewed conflict would be even more damaging than previous rounds of fighting
item.description:
A Democratic-controlled Congress may struggle to ease cost of living pressures and Middle East diplomats warn that renewed conflict between the US and Iran would be even more damaging than previous rounds of fighting. Serbia shuts down a bank favoured by Russians as it enters a new political era. Plus, Binance has started letting customers withdraw funds after the world's biggest crypto exchange experienced a record $6.3bn hack.

item.title: Martin Wolf on the US midterms: What’s the risk of political violence?
item.itunes:title: Martin Wolf on the US midterms: What’s the risk of political violence?
item.itunes:subtitle: Barbara F Walter on why disorder is a risk, but not inevitable
item.description:
As Americans prepare to vote in the November 3 midterm elections, the FT’s chief economics commentator Martin Wolf asks what the result will mean for Donald Trump, the future of US democracy and America's place in the world. In the third of a six-part series, Martin speaks to political scientist and author Barbara F Walter, an expert on civil wars and political violence, about the risk of unrest surrounding the elections. Drawing on her research into countries around the world, Walter explains the warning signs of political violence, and why America's changing demographics and the struggle to hold on to political power are fuelling divisions. How close is the US to a dangerous tipping point? And can American democracy emerge from the midterms stronger rather than more divided?


To enjoy future episodes, be sure to subscribe to ‘Martin Wolf on the World’ wherever you get your podcasts. You can also watch Martin’s podcast series on the FT’s YouTube channel here: https://www.youtube.com/@FinancialTimes


Host: Martin Wolf

Producer: Mischa Frankl-Duval

Senior producers: Laurence Knight and Edwin Lane

Executive producer: Manuela Saragosa

item.title: Alphabet’s brutal day on the stock market
item.itunes:title: Alphabet’s brutal day on the stock market
item.itunes:subtitle: Google owner admits ‘AI mode’ has hurt traditional search as sales and profits undershoot expectations
item.description:
Alphabet’s share price fell just over 12 percent on Thursday, and UK startup Nscale is banking on a troubled US data centre project to underpin its planned $35bn IPO. Plus, we look at what’s next for the ECB now that its president Christine Lagarde announced she’s stepping down.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Alphabet shares tumble in $500bn rout

Inside the make-or-break AI mega-project behind Nscale’s $35bn IPO

item.title: The winners and losers in the UK Budget
item.itunes:title: The winners and losers in the UK Budget
item.itunes:subtitle: Scale of chancellor’s plans was modest compared with recent fiscal events
item.description:
Chancellor John Healey has targeted banks, savers and property owners in his Autumn Budget, Benjamin Netanyahu holds the lead in Israel’s election but there’s no clear winner yet, and one of the oldest American law firms told partners that it should dissolve. Plus, the Federal Reserve kept US borrowing costs on hold days before midterm elections, and Google shares fell sharply after boosting its spending on AI to more than $50bn in the third quarter.


Mentioned in this podcast:

John Healey hits banks and savers with tax rises in Budget ‘for working people’

What’s next for Burnham after the Budget?

item.title: What a local ceasefire means for the Russia-Ukraine war
item.itunes:title: What a local ceasefire means for the Russia-Ukraine war
item.description:
Washington and Moscow are discussing a potential return by American companies to the Russian oil market as a localised ceasefire begins in the Ukrainian town of Oleshky, exit polls suggest there’s no clear winner in the Israel elections, and Brazil’s president is facing down a fiscal reckoning after winning re-election. Plus, China AI stocks are in a bear market, and UK chancellor John Healey will unveil the Autumn Budget.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Washington discusses Russian deals for US oil majors in Ukraine peace talks

Vladimir Putin speaks with Norwegian and Finnish leaders

Russia and Ukraine begin local ceasefire in frontline city

What happens next after Israel’s election?

Lula faces a fiscal reckoning after Brazil’s market rout
